name: Will Haven
label: Revelation
lede: Four Sacramento friends set out to sound like Neurosis and ended up on the road with the Deftones. They broke up after one last night at the Capitol Garage, and have kept coming back since 2005.

eras.title: Three bands for three dollars
eras.text: Will Haven grew out of a Sacramento band called Sock and a scene that ran on Thursday nights at the Cattle Club. Their heroes were Neurosis, Deadguy and Sepultura; the Deftones were down the street, watching.

years.h: Jeff Irwin talks Grady Avenell into the microphone
years.p: Friends since they were 12 or 13, Irwin and Avenell hadn't planned on Avenell fronting anything. He didn't want to sing; Irwin pushed, and with Mike Martin and Wayne Morse they formed Will Haven in Sacramento.
years.xp: The band grew out of a group called Sock. The local hub was the Cattle Club, where Thursdays meant three bands for three dollars, and 924 Gilman Street in Berkeley was a drive away. [[Far|e48fa0b9-7e30-4406-aed2-3605854c9e52]], Deftones and Tinfed were the Sacramento bands they measured themselves against.

years.h: The first Will Haven recording is a six-song demo
years.p: It comes out the year the band forms, and the master cassette has since been transferred and put online.

years.h: The self-titled EP gets Will Haven out of Sacramento
years.p: Will Haven draws positive reviews, and the band starts playing beyond town.

years.h: Will Haven show up in the Deftones' Bored video
years.p: It's a Sacramento cameo, years before the two bands shared stages around the world.

years.h: El Diablo is Will Haven's homage to Neurosis
years.p: The debut album, on Crisis and Revelation, opens with the six-minute Stick Up Kid and closes on the near-nine-minute ¡Escucha!.
years.xp: Eric Stenman engineered and mixed it at The Hangar in Sacramento, the room where the next two records were made too. Revelation, the band says, never asked for a single or a change in sound: being on a hardcore label meant nobody told them what to do.

eras.title: The band the Deftones fought for
eras.text: The Deftones had seen Will Haven form, and once they could pick their openers, they picked them. Those tours led to Soulfly, Fear Factory and Slipknot, and the UK turned out to be especially loud.

years.big: They fought for us to go on tour with them.
years.h: Chino Moreno wants Will Haven on the Deftones' bill
years.p: Wayne Morse, on the Deftones. Singer [[Chino Moreno|e61400d1-9434-4abc-ac7a-4f1dad60cfc7]] had approached Jeff Irwin, then 19, about touring together, and the dates led to Soulfly, Fear Factory and Slipknot.
years.xp: Revelation's own bio also lists opening slots for the [[Beastie Boys|9beb62b2-88db-4cea-801e-162cd344ee53]] and [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]], and tours of California, the East Coast and Europe.

years.h: A song named Jaworski, with Jaworski singing on it
years.p: Jeff Jaworski of Red Tape does backing vocals on the WHVN track named for him. Eric Stenman and the band produced it at The Hangar and The Appliance Shop.
years.xp:
It's REV 79. Revelation pressed the first vinyl run as 1,517 white copies; Music for Nations released it in the UK. Slopez features a drum circle by Adam Federico.

In 2021 Metal Hammer named WHVN one of the 20 best metal albums of 1999.

years.h: Will Haven's turn on the Bad Brains tribute Never Give In
years.p: They cover [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]]' The Regulator.

years.h: Wayne Morse hands the sticks to Mitch Wheeler
years.p: Founding drummer Morse leaves Will Haven, and Wheeler takes over the kit.

years.h: Avenell sings on Soulfly's Pain
years.p: It's one of several guest spots he takes, which also include tracks by [[Far|e48fa0b9-7e30-4406-aed2-3605854c9e52]].

years.h: Carpe Diem reaches No. 24 in the UK
years.p: Through Music for Nations it lands at 24 on the Rock & Metal Albums chart, and the title song hits No. 17 on the rock singles chart. Eric Stenman produces again.
years.xp:
The closer, Moving to Montana, runs almost nine minutes, with a hidden track at 6:15 after twenty seconds of silence. Reviews split hard: Drowned in Sound gave it 9/10, Metal Hammer 5/10. It's REV 104 on Revelation.

The tour behind it took Will Haven across the US, the UK and Japan, plus the Australian Warped Tour.

eras.title: The last night at the Capitol Garage
eras.text: Grady Avenell finished with the Carpe Diem touring and left to go back to school and look after his family. Will Haven played one more hometown show and filmed it.

years.h: Avenell walks away for school and family
years.p: The Carpe Diem touring is done, and he leaves to finish his education and look after his family.

years.h: Will Haven film their last Sacramento show, then go dark
years.p: The Capitol Garage set comes out on DVD as Foreign Films, a title that echoes the El Diablo song Foreign Film.

eras.title: A revolving door at the microphone
eras.text: Will Haven came back in late 2005 with Avenell, then lost him again partway through the comeback record. For two years the singer was the man they'd once named a song after.

years.h: Avenell is back, and so is Will Haven
years.p: The reunion line-up adds drummer Mitch Wheeler and new guitarist Cayle Hunter of Ghostride.

years.big: This is Grady's calling right here.
years.h: Chino Moreno sits in on pre-production in Los Angeles
years.p: Jeff Irwin, hearing Avenell sing again as the band works up its first album since Carpe Diem. Moreno is in the room for the songs.

years.h: Will Haven replace Avenell with the guy they named a song after
years.p: Avenell leaves again after the band records The Hierophant at Bieler Bros. Studios in Pompano Beach, Florida. Jeff Jaworski of Red Tape takes the mic.
years.xp: The Hierophant came out on Bieler Bros. Records. Jaworski had already sung backing vocals on Jaworski, the 1999 WHVN song named after him.

years.cap: Will Haven at the Islington O2 Academy, London, November 2011
years.h: Avenell stays this time
years.p: He rejoins permanently, and Will Haven play benefit shows for Deftones bassist [[Chi Cheng|ed1c0daa-9cdb-4bd8-8f46-794ec0783544]].

years.cap: Will Haven live in Montreal, November 2010
years.h: Slipknot's Chris Fehn picks up the bass
years.p: [[Slipknot|a466c2a2-6517-42fb-a160-1087c3bafd9f]] percussionist [[Chris Fehn|2610ba0c-fe94-4e04-8e15-4b29966afffc]] joins Will Haven, a band Slipknot once toured with. He stays until 2012.

years.cap: Will Haven at the Islington O2 Academy, London, 11 November 2011
years.h: Voir Dire is album number five
years.p: It comes out on Bieler Bros. in the US and on the UK's Holy Roar.

years.h: Adrien Contreras takes over on bass
years.p: He replaces Fehn and is still in the band today.

eras.title: Thirty years of WHVN
eras.text: Settled at last, Will Haven made records on their own schedule for Minus Head Records, filmed a sequel to the breakup DVD, and went back out to play Carpe Diem for the people who grew up on it.

years.h: Open the Mind to Discomfort comes out on Artery
years.p: It's a four-year gap since Voir Dire, and it's an EP.

years.h: Muerte starts the Minus Head years
years.p: It's Will Haven's sixth album and their first for Minus Head Records.

years.h: Foreign Films II follows the first by 19 years
years.p: The documentary covers regrouping and making Muerte. Jeff Irwin says it has the feel of the original, from a more mature band.

years.h: VII gets a tour paired with Carpe Diem
years.p: It was recorded at Pus Cavern in Sacramento with Joe Johnston, partly through the pandemic. Sean Bivins joins on keys and guitar.
years.xp: The August US tour played the new album alongside Carpe Diem. UK and French dates followed in October 2023.

years.h: Thirty years in, No Stars to Guide Me
years.p: The single KIRE arrives ahead of the 30th-anniversary compilation on Minus Head.
